Prevention: Use disease-free planting material available from
FOHCREC Kade or a certified nursery
Timely and complete harvesting of ripe fruit to reduce disease inoculum
Removal and burial of fallen fruit from the orchrd floor helps to reduce disease inoculum. and burning of leaves from the orchard floor reduces the source of inoculum and therefore the disease
Prune to remove unproductive and diseased branches after harvest to reduce humidity and increase air circulation in the orchard to reduce the disease
Encourage other citrus farmers in the area to have a routine management programme
Monitoring: In areas where the disease is present, start a preventative fungicide regime after petal drop.
Infection occurs when the fruits are young but symptoms don't appear until maturity
To detect symptoms of the disease, look at the underside of fallen decomposing leaves every month for the presence of minute black spots using a hand lens.
These are the fruiting bodies which produce the infective spores
Monitor fruit for symptoms close to maturity, including small hard sunken brown/ black spots
Direct Control: There are no green direct controls for this disease
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
